fatal_errors: The proposed system and intervention do not reconstruct the target: it substitutes an additively manufactured gamma-prime-strengthened HEA and post-solution cooling-rate change for as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 aged across 550–750°C.

The proposed mechanism concerns precipitate-induced serrated grain boundaries and resistance to intergranular cracking, whereas the target mechanism is plastic instability caused by enhanced L12 ordering, elevated APBE, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, and stress concentration at jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary tips.
It does not predict the target non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition, including minimum ductility near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.

The experiment does not isolate grain-boundary serration from correlated changes in precipitate size, grain size, and precipitation strengthening, so improved properties would not uniquely establish the proposed causal mediator.
explanation: The response is a coherent and directly evidence-supported alternative hypothesis about toughness retention in an SLM-produced HEA. E1–E3 support slow-cooling-induced gamma-prime coarsening, Zener-drag-generated grain-boundary serration, more uniform strain, and improved fracture strain and creep life. Its controlled comparison and mediator/property measurements are testable, although direct crack-path or local-strain measurements and a design separating precipitate coarsening from boundary serration would improve causal discrimination. Relative to the hidden paper, however, nearly all material-specific elements differ: alloy state, thermal intervention, relevant boundaries, deformation mechanism, baseline, and predicted temperature dependence. The stated boundary is also broad and qualitative, and the falsification rule partly treats failure of the intervention to create serrations as falsification of the serration mechanism. Thus it is scientifically plausible and well sourced, but not a reconstruction of the target result.
